rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Carbon monoxide is colourless, odourless and tasteless.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: It can be produced when fuels burn without enough oxygen.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Carbon monoxide enters the blood through the lungs.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: It binds to haemoglobin and reduces oxygen delivery to tissues and organs.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: High indoor concentrations can be fatal.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Lower-level exposure can cause symptoms resembling flu, viral illness or food poisoning.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Common symptoms include headache, dizziness, nausea, weakness and confusion.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Chest pain, breathlessness, collapse or loss of consciousness can indicate serious exposure.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: People with conditions affecting oxygen delivery to the heart or brain can be especially vulnerable.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: If exposure is suspected, people should move away from the source and get into fresh air if safe.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: People who feel unwell after suspected exposure should seek medical advice.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Severe symptoms or immediate danger require emergency assistance.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Symptoms can improve after leaving the source, but medical assessment can still be necessary.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Relevant rented homes in England require a carbon-monoxide alarm in rooms with fixed combustion appliances, excluding gas cookers.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Relevant landlords must repair or replace prescribed alarms after being informed and finding them faulty.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Alarm type and location should follow the building, occupant needs and manufacturer instructions.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Carbon-monoxide alarms supplement safe installation, maintenance and ventilation.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Carbon-monoxide symptoms are non-specific and diagnosis requires clinical assessment and exposure history.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: An alarm does not prove that an appliance, flue or ventilation system is safe.

rows.source: UKHSA, NHS and housing carbon-monoxide guidance
rows.verified: Carbon-monoxide guidance is health and housing context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
